correctness.rationale: Cuts containing F are exactly binary proper colorings of (V,F); bipartite components independently flip, giving forced odd paths; nonbipartite F implies vacuous complete closure. Triple path-shortcut plus triangle rules generate the full closure. For one-pass rules, every forced edge is witnessed by an odd simple path length <=D, or inconsistent F contains an odd cycle <=D except the Hamiltonian odd-cycle case where any missing edge is a chord with an odd arc <=D. A D-edge odd cycle and isolated outsider force an edge that no proper subset forces. A 3-edge path has no proper 2-edge nontrivial implication. Standalone exhaustive n=4,5,6 and further odd-cycle witnesses match the theorem; those experiments are not relied on for infinite correctness.
